character: Best: the founder, a professional quantity surveyor, in his own voice, recorded on a decent USB or lapel mic in a quiet office (this is the deep-dive and the standing link for demo follow-ups). Fallback (AI): the same mid-career Kiwi QS voice as 'Six bids. Six formats.', 'Why six bids never compare' and 'Action: chase painter' (late 30s to 40s, general urban New Zealand accent, not broad, not Australian). Calm and dry, a colleague walking a developer through what a lender actually reads. Explaining, never selling. An AI voice never speaks as the founder and is never captioned as him.
casting_line: Your programme. As the lender sees it. One contract, counted six times. Q-S-me dot build.
series_rule: The burned-in captions and the big hook/title type are the subtitles, so every voiced line is read word for word ('A4' is read 'A-four', '30-minute' is read 'thirty-minute'). Chapter numbers are spoken with the card title. Sticky notes, chips, toasts and product wording on the screens are not captions and stay unvoiced.
time_base: Seconds on outputs/a-programme-a-lender-can-read-16x9.mp4 (128.1 s). The page is authored on a 132.5 s clock and an edit list (motion/lender.js → SKIPS/HOLDS) maps the file onto it: the title's hold and the middle of every chapter card are cut, chapter 3 holds three still frames for its captions, and two long holds in chapter 5 are cut. These are real file times (window.__toReal(authored) converts).
continuous_read_v2:
Your programme. As the lender sees it.

No dates on the bars.

It runs off the page.

One contract, counted six times.

So what's actually holding this build up?

A programme a lender can read.

Six fixes. One printout.

One. From the estimate.

Start from what you priced.

Each job brings its own days.

Even the rain flag comes across.

Then you link what waits for what.

Two. Slips and rain.

One slip moves what's linked.

Anyone booked is asked, not told.

Nothing changes for them until they say yes.

Rained off? See what moves before you push.

Three. What drives the finish.

Purple decides the finish date.

Grey has room.

The painter everyone chased? Never purple.

Purple slips a day, the finish slips a day.

Four. Your days off.

This one runs straight through the site's own shutdown.

Your holidays and shutdowns? Add them as days off.

Work moves later. Never earlier.

Mid-January was never real.

Five. Money, once.

Estimates carry a squiggle. Agreed prices don't.

And a contract counts once, not six times.

Paid is what's been recorded as paid.

Six. Print it.

The whole chart fits across the A-four.

The task list follows.

Dates in words, on every bar.

When, how long, how much. Up top.

And the lender's question, answered in one sentence.

On your letterhead.

Bring your current programme to a thirty-minute demo. Q-S-me dot build.
